canDo.en: I can recognise and use understatement, irony and implied criticism, and I can read a writer's real attitude when it differs from the literal meaning of their words.
canDo.bg: Мога да разпознавам и използвам недоизказване, ирония и скрита критика и да разчитам истинското отношение на автора, когато то се различава от буквалния смисъл на думите му.

body.en: English speakers, especially British ones, often express strong views by saying less than they mean. "It wasn't exactly cheap" means it was very expensive; "I've had better" means it was poor; "That could have gone better" after a disaster is an understatement. Litotes uses a negative to affirm the opposite: "not bad" (= quite good), "not unlike" (= similar to), "no small achievement" (= a big achievement). Taking these literally — or answering them literally — is a classic way for even advanced learners to misread tone. Bulgarian has similar devices ("не е зле"), but they are less frequent and less loaded.
body.bg: Носителите на английския, особено британците, често изразяват силни мнения, като казват по-малко, отколкото мислят. "It wasn't exactly cheap" значи, че е било много скъпо; "I've had better" значи, че е било слабо; "That could have gone better" след провал е недоизказване. Литотата използва отрицание, за да утвърди обратното: "not bad" (= доста добре), "not unlike" (= подобен на), "no small achievement" (= голямо постижение). Буквалното тълкуване — или буквален отговор — е класически начин дори напреднали да разчетат тона погрешно. В българския има подобни похвати ("не е зле"), но са по-редки и по-малко натоварени.

examples: Finishing a marathon at seventy is no small achievement.
Well, that could have gone better.
The new design is not unlike the old one.

body.en: Irony says the opposite of, or something very different from, what is meant, and relies on the listener to notice the gap: "Oh, wonderful — another meeting". In writing, it is often signalled by over-precise or overly formal praise ("a mere fifty minutes"), by damning with faint praise ("the parking was excellent" as the only compliment for a hotel), or by a pointed short sentence after a quotation ("It was certainly bold"). Implied criticism also hides in polite formulas: "With respect…" often introduces disagreement, and "I hear what you're saying" may mean "I don't accept it". To read tone, ask: is the literal meaning plausible in this context?
body.bg: Иронията казва обратното или нещо много различно от това, което се има предвид, и разчита слушателят да забележи разминаването: "Oh, wonderful — another meeting". Писмено тя често се сигнализира с прекалено прецизна или прекалено официална похвала ("a mere fifty minutes"), с "убийствено сдържана похвала" ("the parking was excellent" като единствен комплимент за хотел) или с кратко, остро изречение след цитат ("It was certainly bold"). Скритата критика се крие и в учтиви формули: "With respect…" често въвежда несъгласие, а "I hear what you're saying" може да значи "Не го приемам". За да разчетеш тона, питай се: правдоподобен ли е буквалният смисъл в този контекст?

texts.title: Restaurant review: The Gilded Fork
paragraphs: The Gilded Fork opened last month to considerable fanfare, and it is not hard to see where the money went. The dining room is a triumph of velvet and brass; one could happily spend an evening admiring the light fittings, which is fortunate, because you may well have to.

Our first courses arrived a mere fifty minutes after we ordered. The scallops were, to be fair, perfectly pleasant, though I suspect they would have been more pleasant still had they been warm. The lamb was described by our waiter as "a bold reinterpretation". It was certainly bold.
Dessert, a deconstructed lemon tart, had been deconstructed so thoroughly that some of its components appeared never to have been introduced to one another.
Service, it must be said, was unfailingly courteous, if somewhat elusive. Our waiter apologised twice for the delay and once, rather touchingly, for the lamb.

At ninety pounds a head before wine, the Gilded Fork is not exactly a bargain. Still, I am told the chef has ambitious plans. I wish him every success with them, and I shall wait, with some patience, to see how they turn out.

items.prompt: A friend comes back from a holiday in Switzerland and says: "Well, it wasn't exactly cheap." What does she mean?
options: The prices were reasonable.
It was quite cheap, but not very cheap.
She doesn't remember the prices.
It was very expensive.

explanation.en: "Not exactly + positive adjective" is a common understatement that usually means the opposite, strongly: not exactly cheap = very expensive. The mild wording makes the point more humorously.
explanation.bg: "Not exactly + положително прилагателно" е често недоизказване, което обикновено означава силно обратното: not exactly cheap = много скъпо. Мекият изказ прави забележката по-хумористична.

hints.en: This is an understatement. Think of the strong opposite.
hints.bg: Това е недоизказване. Помисли за силното обратно.

items.prompt: "Getting both parties to sign the agreement was no small achievement." What is the speaker saying?
options: The achievement was minor.
It was a significant achievement.
It was not an achievement at all.
The agreement was small.

explanation.en: "No small achievement" is litotes: denying the opposite to emphasise the point. It means a considerable achievement, and it often sounds more admiring than simply saying "a big achievement".
explanation.bg: "No small achievement" е литота: отрича се обратното, за да се подчертае казаното. Значи значително постижение и често звучи по-възхитено от простото "a big achievement".

items.prompt: Your colleague reads an email, sighs, and says: "Oh, wonderful. The deadline's been moved forward again." How does she feel?
options: Delighted that the work will finish sooner.
Indifferent; it's just information.
Annoyed — "wonderful" is ironic.
Confused about the new date.

explanation.en: The sigh and the situation (an earlier deadline is usually bad news) show that "wonderful" is ironic and means the opposite. "Again" adds to the frustration.
explanation.bg: Въздишката и ситуацията (по-ранен краен срок обикновено е лоша новина) показват, че "wonderful" е иронично и значи обратното. "Again" засилва раздразнението.

hints.en: Is a deadline moving forward usually good news?
hints.bg: Обикновено добра новина ли е, когато срокът се изтегли по-рано?

items.sentence: A: How was the concert? B: Hmm. I've ___ better.

explanation.en: "I've had better" (or "heard better", "seen better", "been to better") is a mild-sounding way to say something was poor. The speaker avoids saying "It was bad" directly but makes their opinion clear.
explanation.bg: "I've had better" (или "heard better", "seen better", "been to better") е меко звучащ начин да кажеш, че нещо е било слабо. Говорещият избягва прякото "It was bad", но мнението му е ясно.

items.prompt: An online review of a hotel says only: "The car park was spacious and well lit." What is the reviewer most likely implying?
options: There was little else worth praising about the hotel.
The reviewer only used the car park.
The hotel was excellent overall.
The hotel is mainly a car park.

explanation.en: Praising a minor, peripheral feature and ignoring the essentials (rooms, service, food) is "damning with faint praise": the silence about everything else is the criticism.
explanation.bg: Да похвалиш второстепенна подробност и да премълчиш основното (стаи, обслужване, храна) е "damning with faint praise": мълчанието за всичко останало е критиката.

hints.en: What does the review NOT mention?

objective.en: Read implied disagreement in a polite formula.
objective.bg: Да разчетеш скрито несъгласие в учтива формула.

items.prompt: In a debate, a politician begins: "With the greatest respect to my honourable colleague…" What is probably coming next?
options: Strong agreement with the colleague.
A thank-you speech.
A change of topic.
A firm disagreement or criticism.

explanation.en: Paradoxically, "With (the greatest) respect…" is a conventional signal that the speaker is about to disagree strongly. The more elaborate the respect, the sharper the disagreement tends to be.
explanation.bg: Парадоксално, "With (the greatest) respect…" е утвърден сигнал, че говорещият ще изрази силно несъгласие. Колкото по-изящно е уважението, толкова по-остро обикновено е несъгласието.

hints.en: Polite formulas don't always mean what they say.
hints.bg: Учтивите формули не винаги значат буквално това, което казват.

accept: Well, that could have gone better.

explanation.en: Said after an obvious failure, this is classic British understatement: everyone knows it went badly, and the dry wording acknowledges this with humour.
explanation.bg: Казано след очевиден провал, това е класическо британско недоизказване: всички знаят, че е минало зле, а сухата формулировка го признава с хумор.

items.prompt: "One could happily spend an evening admiring the light fittings, which is fortunate, because you may well have to." What is the reviewer's point?
options: The service is so slow that you'll have plenty of time with nothing to do but look at the décor.
The lighting is the best feature, and the food is equally good.
The restaurant is too dark to see the food.
Diners are encouraged to stay all evening.

explanation.en: The sentence begins as praise and then turns: "which is fortunate, because you may well have to" implies you will have nothing else to do — a sharp hint at slow service, confirmed by the "mere fifty minutes" wait in the next paragraph.
explanation.bg: Изречението започва като похвала и после рязко се обръща: "which is fortunate, because you may well have to" намеква, че няма да имаш какво друго да правиш — остър намек за бавно обслужване, потвърден от чакането "a mere fifty minutes" в следващия абзац.

hints.en: Why would you HAVE TO look at the lights all evening?
hints.bg: Защо би ТРЯБВАЛО да гледаш лампите цяла вечер?

objective.en: Recognise irony created by a single word.
objective.bg: Да разпознаеш ирония, създадена с една дума.

items.prompt: In "Our first courses arrived a mere fifty minutes after we ordered", what is the effect of "a mere"?
options: It shows that fifty minutes is a reasonable wait.
It shows the reviewer is uncertain about the time.
It ironically presents a very long wait as if it were short.
It suggests the food arrived too early.

explanation.en: "A mere" normally minimises something (a mere five euros). Applying it to an excessive wait makes the complaint ironic and sharper than a direct statement like "We waited far too long".
explanation.bg: "A mere" обикновено омаловажава нещо (a mere five euros = едва пет евро). Приложено към прекалено дълго чакане, прави оплакването иронично и по-остро от прякото "We waited far too long".

hints.en: Is fifty minutes for a starter short or long?
hints.bg: Петдесет минути за предястие кратко ли е, или дълго?

items.sentence: The reviewer uses understatement about the price, saying the restaurant is not exactly a ___.

explanation.en: The last paragraph: "At ninety pounds a head before wine, the Gilded Fork is not exactly a bargain." Like "not exactly cheap", this means it is very overpriced — especially given the rest of the review.
explanation.bg: Последният абзац: "At ninety pounds a head before wine, the Gilded Fork is not exactly a bargain." Като "not exactly cheap", това значи, че е силно надценено — особено на фона на останалото ревю.
